task: Rank the real, demonstrated routes to restoring movement after spinal cord injury (SCI): (a) intracortical BCI + FES reanimation (Bouton 2016 NeuroLife, Ajiboye 2017), (b) epidural/transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation restoring standing/stepping (Harkema, Angeli, Gill/Calvert Mayo, Wagner/Courtine 2018), (c) the brain-spine 'digital bridge' (Lorach/Courtine 2023), (d) nerve/axon regeneration + regenerative adjuncts. Forced adversary held OPEN and honest: real functional independence in daily life, or small-n lab demonstrations with tethered equipment.
confidence_tier: TIERED. (1) HIGHEST -- all 15 PMIDs live-verified this session via NCBI eutils esearch->esummary->efetch, direct abstract quotes used for every quantitative claim (n, injury level, functional outcome); the INSPIRE single-arm-vs-RCT contrast (#13 vs #14) is a machine-checkable, textbook forced-adversary kill with exact matched-endpoint numbers (44% vs 20%-vs-30%-control at the same 6-month timepoint). (2) STRONG -- the multi-group SCS convergence (4 independent groups/institutions -- Louisville, Mayo, Lausanne, Seattle -- across 2 countries, implanted AND non-invasive) on standing/stepping restoration in chronic motor-complete SCI, forced against the Fawcett 2007 spontaneous-recovery void-floor plus within-subject ON/OFF causal contrasts built into the original case reports. (3) WEAKEST, disclosed -- Wagner 2018's own abstract does not state its participant count; the digital-bridge and both BCI+FES results are n=1 case studies, real but not yet independently replicated; Inanici 2021's 'matched or exceeded implanted stimulation' is the source paper's own comparative claim, not an independently-run head-to-head trial.

pathway_geometry.graph: M1(cortex) --CST(white matter)--> LSN(spinal interneurons+motoneuron pool) --peripheral nerve--> NMJ --> MUSCLE
pathway_geometry.sci_lesion: cuts the CST EDGE at the injury level; M1 and LSN/muscle nodes are each typically anatomically intact but disconnected (matches the UMN-lesion mechanism already quantified in MECHANISM_CORTICOSPINAL_MOTOR_COMMAND.md via Doherty et al. 2002)
pathway_geometry.method_a_bci_fes: new edge M1--[decode+wire]-->MUSCLE directly; full bypass of the LSN and peripheral pathway; needs NO spared tissue below the cut (works even at AIS A)
pathway_geometry.method_b_scs: no new edge from M1; raises gain/excitability of the existing LSN node itself; needs SOME spared CST fraction or intact afferent-feedback loop (Angeli 2014 mechanistic finding)
pathway_geometry.method_c_digital_bridge: new edge M1--[decode+wire]-->LSN (not muscle); reconstructs the missing CST edge itself into the still-intact LSN->NMJ->MUSCLE machinery; topologically closest to the original intact graph
pathway_geometry.method_d_nerve_transfer: new edge at the peripheral-nerve tier only, downstream of the lesion entirely; reroutes an intact-but-spare donor nerve (fed by an uninjured UMN path at a different segment) into denervated MUSCLE; never touches the CST edge or the lesion itself
pathway_geometry.unresolved_edge: true CNS axon regeneration THROUGH the lesion/glial scar itself (method d3, scaffold) -- the one edge nobody has yet rebuilt in a human at the function level; INSPIRE 2.0 RCT found no benefit

overall_verdict: No approach today gives a person with complete, chronic SCI unassisted, hardware-free, normal walking or hand function at population scale, on demand. Nerve-transfer surgery restores genuinely independent, permanent, hardware-free upper-limb function for appropriate cervical candidates only, never gait. Epidural/transcutaneous SCS is the best-replicated real effect (4 independent groups) restoring standing/stepping/walking well beyond the natural-recovery window, but remains implant-and-usually-walker-dependent. The digital bridge delivered the single most complete real-world independence demonstration (explicit >1-year home use) for one person, unreplicated. Intracortical BCI+FES restores real, richly dexterous, cortically-driven control of a person's own paralyzed limb for specific tasks, but has never been shown outside a monitored research session in either landmark trial. Regenerative medicine for the lesion itself is not yet a functional-restoration method -- the one rigorously randomized trial found no benefit over standard surgical care.
honest_gaps: Wagner 2018 (PMID 30382197) participant count not confirmed via its own abstract text this session; commonly reported n=3 (STIMO trial) disclosed as recalled, not independently reconfirmed.
No take-home/community-use BCI+FES (method a) trial was found live this session for either landmark system -- absence is the finding (claim_a), search not exhaustive of all grey literature.
Curtis 2018 (PMID 29859175) is explicitly underpowered by its own authors' statement -- used only at the confidence tier its authors assign it.

INSPIRE 2.0 (PMID 39471088)'s null result is itself from a small trial (n=20, 10/arm) -- symmetric caveat: could in principle be under-powered, though the point estimate ran in the unfavorable direction for the scaffold (the conservative direction for this specific adversary).

Gorman & Mortimer 1983 (PMID 6604691) is a pre-abstract-era record -- title/journal/DOI confirmed live, no abstract text exists; the reverse-recruitment mechanism cited is classically-established electrophysiology, flagged as recalled-not-requoted.
Inanici 2021 (PMID 33400652)'s 'matched or exceeded implanted stimulation' is the source paper's own comparative textual claim, not an independently-run head-to-head trial.

No in-repo simulation or live-computed number was produced this session -- every figure is a literature citation, machine-cross-checked against source abstract text. Tier: literature-anchored HYPOTHESIS, not a MEASURED cell.
